criteria.note: Step 2 collects structured absence data — last day worked and first day absent as date inputs, a bounded nature-of-absence selector, and a free-text details field — and employment context (occupation, division, hire date) is carried in the member panel. Submit is blocked until a member has been identified and all three absence fields are set. Caveat: `identified` is a sticky flag; editing policy-number or member-id after a successful lookup does not clear it, so a submission can pair edited identifiers with the previously looked-up member's name and plan.

Attestation checkbox in step 4 whose wording explicitly names "the member and plan details shown above ... as pre-populated and corrected". The submit handler pushes 'confirm the attestation' onto `problems` when unchecked, and any non-empty `problems` list aborts before a reference is generated, so the attestation genuinely gates acceptance. Pre-populated fields are plain editable inputs, not readonly, so "corrected" is real.

The file input carries `multiple`, and selections accumulate into one `attachments` array rather than replacing it — `docsInput.value = ''` after each change is what makes a second selection additive. Duplicates are suppressed by name+size. The packet is rendered as one list with per-file removal, at least one document is required to submit, and the confirmation reports the packet as a count plus the full file-name list.

Both checks run before `attachments.push`, so a rejected file never enters the packet and nothing partial is held. The message is specific — it names each rejected file, the reason (type vs. "over the 10 MB limit" with the actual size), states that nothing from a rejected file has been kept, restates the policy, and reports how many documents remain — and renders in the error style. Mixed batches correctly keep the valid files. Enforcement is client-side only, which is inherent to a static page but is not a policy boundary.

On a clean submit the form and intro are hidden and the confirmation section is revealed in-page with no navigation or network round trip, carrying a tick, "Claim submission received", a Status: Received badge, a monospace reference in `MS-YYYY-MM-NNNN` form generated at submit time, and a summary of member, policy/plan, absence, documents and timestamp. Reference format is quotable; see notes on its uniqueness and on what it actually refers to.

notes: The 6 passing tests are string matching against index.html as text — no DOM, no browser, no execution. Several assert exact source lines (e.g. `if (!identified) { problems.push('look up the member'); }` and `setMsg(uploadMsg, 'Not attached: '`). They therefore evidence that the code is present, not that it behaves: the AC4 test proves the rejection branches exist as text, never that a bad file is actually rejected. They are also brittle to any reformatting, and would keep passing if the handler were never wired to an element. I verified the criteria by reading the implementation directly rather than relying on the suite.

Stale identification: `identified` is set on a successful lookup and cleared only on a failed one. Change the policy number or member ID afterwards without re-running the lookup and the confirmation shows the edited identifiers next to the original member's name and plan — the sponsor then attests to a combination that was never resolved against a record. Clearing `identified` on input to policy-number/member-id would close it.

The confirmation asserts effects that do not occur: "MapleSure intake has your packet" and "A copy has been placed in your SponsorConnect submissions list". Nothing is transmitted, stored, or listed anywhere — there is no backend and no submissions list. The page-level demo banner covers the environment, but per the project's staged-output rule these two specific sentences state a completed action that did not happen and should be reworded or badged.

The reference number's uniqueness rests on `Math.floor(1000 + Math.random() * 9000)` — 9,000 values scoped per year-month, so collisions are likely across a demo session and the reference resolves to no persisted record.
Minor hygiene: `__pycache__/` (a .pyc) is present in the produced artifact directory alongside index.html and test_app.py.
